author: Engelbert Kaempfer; trans. J. G. Scheuchzer
frontispiece_type: engraved additional title/frontispiece using Japanese heraldic insignia
notes: International Research Center for Japanese Studies lists a formal frontispiece; Folger describes it as an additional engraved title, 'Historia imperii Japonici'. Kaempfer/Scheuchzer's own introduction states that several coats of arms and insignia of the Japanese emperor, princes and nobility were engraved in the frontispiece. Preserve the hybrid frontispiece/additional-title status rather than forcing it into a single modern category.

author: Edward Long
work: The History of Jamaica; or, General Survey of the Antient and Modern State of the Island
artist_or_engraver: cartographers/engravers vary; vol. I chart associated with Thomas Kitchin
notes: Wellcome explicitly collates folded frontispieces in vols. I-II; Christie's independently records two folding frontispiece maps. Yale identifies the map unfolded at the opening of vol. I as 'A Chart of the Environs of Jamaica, including its Dependencies' (1774). This is a strong case of territorial/cartographic framing replacing portrait or allegory.

author: Bryan Edwards
work: The History, Civil and Commercial, of the British Colonies in the West Indies
artist_or_engraver: engravers to normalize; Thomas Stothard/W. Grainger belong to separate Sable Venus plate, not these formal frontispieces
notes: Contemporary/rare-book collation gives an engraved frontispiece in each volume. Vol. I depicts an Indigenous cacique of Cuba addressing Columbus on a future state; vol. II depicts Columbus and his sons Diego and Ferdinand, pointing over charts/globe toward voyages and discovery. Crucial exclusion: binder directions place 'The Voyage of the Sable Venus from Angola to the West Indies' at vol. II p. 27, not as the formal volume frontispiece, despite later catalogues sometimes calling that famous plate a frontispiece.

author: Archibald Dalzel
work: The History of Dahomy, an Inland Kingdom of Africa
publisher: T. Spilsbury and Son for the editor / author issues
notes: Wellcome's copy is catalogued with a folded map as frontispiece plus six further plates; a specialist collation independently gives 'folding map as frontis'. Folger shows two 1793 issue statements (editor/J. Evans and author/Nicol-Dilly-Richardson), so issue-level imprint should remain explicit if copies are compared.
